messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: high - Network: multiple failed health checks in us-east-1a. Potential regional routing anomalies. Please acknowledge.
priya: acked. I'm oncall. Looking at monitoring — heading to the dashboard now.
marco: I see a surge of DNS lookup errors from our regional probes, 10:12-10:14 UTC window. Could be a cloud AZ routing flap.
priya: telemetry for the region looks partial — our agent count drops in the middle of the window. Some probes show 0 samples. Suspect missing heartbeat.
liu: operator note: cloud provider posted a NIC-level maintenance at 10:05 in us-east-1a, not flagged as outage. Could be correlated.
priya: are customers impacted? Any 5xx or elevated latency on inference gateways in that AZ?
marco: checking metrics: 99.9% of inference traffic already multi-AZ; a small subset of pinned Dedicated hosts returned connection resets. Logging shows error paths to us-east-1a endpoints.
priya: runbook step 1: confirm if it's real or false positive. I can run the probe from a control plane host.
alyssa: FYI I got the same PD page. Some synthetic checks failed but regional LB health still reporting green.
priya: running curl to a few endpoints and DNS from our control node:```bash
dig +short model-api.use1.redwood-inference.test @8.8.8.8
curl -v https://model-api.use1.redwood-inference.test/health
```
priya: dig returns inconsistent answers — some queries time out. curl shows TLS handshake reset occasionally.
marco: can you paste a sample tcpdump from the probe host? suspect packet loss to that AZ subnet.
priya: grabbing 15s tcpdump (sanitized):```text
10:12:03 IP control-1 > api-gw.use1a: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460], length 0
10:12:03 IP api-gw.use1a > control-1: RST, seq 1, win 0, length 0
10:12:04 IP control-1 > api-gw.use1a: Flags [S], retransmit
```
liu: those RSTs align with NIC-level device logs I can see via cloud console. Provider hints about brief BGP reconvergence for that AZ.
priya: this is starting to look like a regional networking hiccup, not our app-level issue. But our monitoring is weird — some probe telemetry missing which made the alert noisy.
marco: agree. We should suppress noisy probe alerts and page only if customer-facing metrics breach thresholds. I'll mute the synthetic probe alert rule for us-east-1a for 30m while we validate.
priya: doing a quick mitigation: move affected pinned hosts off the us-east-1a affinity group to multi-AZ pool to avoid restarts for customers. Initiating migration for two dedicated nodes now.
deploy-bot: devops: migration job started for host-id ded-0452 -> target-pool multi-az-1. Job 7892.
alyssa: how many customers on those hosts? Any high-SLA ones?
marco: two mid-market customers, both on dedicated plans but not enterprise SLA. I'll notify customers via status page if we keep them moved.
priya: paging update for oncall handoff: I'll be available for the next 40m then hand to Marco for the rest of shift. Please add notes to the incident channel.
marco: I'll take watch after 40m. Meanwhile I'm asking observability team to investigate why our probe agents dropped telemetry during the same window — might be a heartbeat aggregation bug under partial network partition.
liu: opened cloud-support ticket referencing NIC and BGP reconverge with their incident id: CS-4621. Provider acknowledges potential transient routing issue in us-east-1a between 10:05-10:20 UTC.
priya: customer impact summary for status: "We observed intermittent network errors affecting a small fraction of inference requests routed to us-east-1a between 10:05-10:20 UTC. Most traffic was served from other AZs; a small number of dedicated hosts experienced transient restarts. No data loss detected. We're mitigating by moving affected hosts and working with the cloud provider."
marco: agree. I'll post that to status.redwood and tag customers on the two dedicated hosts.
alyssa: deploy-bot shows migration success for ded-0452, pending ded-0467.
deploy-bot: migration job 7892 completed for ded-0452. migration job 7893 started for ded-0467.
priya: probes are slowly recovering in monitoring; heartbeat counts back to normal at 10:26 UTC. I'm lifting the mute in 10m and will watch for recurrence.
marco: follow-up items: (1) add guard in alert rule to require both probe failure AND customer-facing 5xx/latency spike, (2) investigate heartbeat aggregation code for edge case of partial partition, (3) include provider maintenance events into our alert correlation pipeline.
priya: noted. I'll create the three action items in our post-incident board with owners.
liu: cloud support closed CS-4621 as "transient, resolved" at 10:30 UTC.
priya: handing off fully to Marco now — leaving watch. Marco, please escalate to oncall lead if it recurs.
marco: taking watch. Leaving brief log in the incident thread for runbook and mitigation steps. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
